Mitchell]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Olympia Snowe]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsME}} The '''1994 United States Senate election in Maine''' was held November 8, 1994. Incumbent Democratic U.S. Senator and Senate Majority Leader [[George J. Mitchell]] decided to retire, instead of seeking a third full term. [[United States House of Representatives|Congressman]] [[Thomas Andrews (American politician)|Tom Andrews]] won the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] primary unopposed, while [[United States House of Representatives|Congresswoman]] [[Olympia Snowe]] won the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] primary unopposed. Snowe was not challenging Mitchell for his Senate seat: she ran for the seat when it became open upon his retirement announcement on March 3rd, 1994. In the general election, Snowe defeated Andrews in a rout to win her first of three terms in the [[United States Senate]], a stark contrast to retiring Senator Mitchell's landslide win [[1988 United States Senate election in Maine|six years prior]].
